Live transcript

  1. ThemQuestionLet's start with a recent project. Which part was yours?
  2. MeI owned the caching layer of the order service. We moved the hot queries from the database to Redis.
  3. ThemOkay, that's a big piece.
  4. ThemQuestionSo when the database and the cache both change, how do you keep them consistent?
  5. MeWe update the database first, then delete the cache…
  6. ThemQuestionAnd if deleting the cache fails?

Heard on this Mac only

Suggested answer

2/2

So when the database and the cache both change, how do you keep them consistent?

We write to the database first, then delete the cache entry, and a binlog subscriber backs that up. It's eventually consistent.

  • After a successful write we delete the key; a read that misses goes to the database and refills the cache.
  • If the delete fails, the key goes to a retry queue, and the binlog subscriber deletes it again.
  • Hot keys get a delayed double delete, so a stale value has almost no time to sneak back in.
  • Where we need strong consistency, like balances, we read from the database or take a distributed lock.

Notes only: no automatic answers. Press ⇧⌘↩ when you need help, or type a question below.

Based on: Materials 2

Question by question
  1. 1

    What if deleting the cache fails? [18:22] Good

    My answer: Retry queue plus an async delete from the binlog. Two safety nets.

  2. 2

    A hot key expires and a flood of requests hits the database at once. What do you do? [27:05] To improve

    My answer: Add a lock… (8-second pause) …maybe a Bloom filter.

    Better answer

    Answer first: a mutex rebuild or logical expiry, chosen by how fresh the data must be. A Bloom filter stops penetration, not breakdown; keep them apart.

№ 04Audio

Whatever app the call is in,
it doesn’t need to know.

On a call, it listens to whatever your Mac plays, plus your microphone: them on one channel, you on the other. In one room together, it uses the microphone alone and calls it “Room”.

ThemEverything this Mac plays · Zoom, Teams, Meet or a browser tab, all the same

MeMicrophone

RoomMicrophone only; everyone in the room is on this one channel

  1. ThemWalk me through your rollout plan on the next slide.
  2. MeSure. We ramp up in three batches.
  1. RoomSam, can you have the data filled in by Thursday?
  2. RoomThen let's move the review to next Monday.
  • Heard on this Mac. Never recorded.
  • Music or a video playing too? Narrow it to a single window.
  • In person it just takes notes; a task only goes to someone named out loud.

№ 05Notes

After the call,
notes you can send
as they are.

Answers in the moment are about speed; notes can take their time. After you end the call it works quietly, and a few minutes later the notes are on the same page, ready to send.

    Proofread

    “we moved the hot queries to Redis”

    Run regression tests and report results [05:40]

    Check

    Nothing nobody said. “Due Thursday” becomes a date; anything unclear is marked “To confirm”.

    Thursday → Thu 29 Oct To confirm

three kinds of notes.

№ 08FAQ

Questions people ask.

Will the other side know?

It never sends anything into the meeting; it only shows things on your screen or phone. If you share your whole screen, the prompt on it may be seen, so move the answers to your phone. Whether and how to use it is up to the rules of the room.

Does it work with any meeting app?

Yes. It listens to what your Mac plays, so it never needs to know which app the call is in.

What if we’re all in one room?

Choose In person and it uses the microphone alone, labelling the transcript “Room”. The notes only put a task on someone who was named out loud.

Does it keep recordings?

No. The sound becomes text on your Mac and is gone; only the transcript and notes stay.

I just want notes, no prompting.

Press Record now. It listens quietly through the meeting, and a few minutes after, the notes are on the page.

Is it in English?

Yes, English and Chinese. Answers follow the conversation, so an English interview gets English answers.
